glossary.Bile duct: Tube carrying bile from the liver and gallbladder into the duodenum.
glossary.Biliary obstruction: Blockage of bile flow anywhere along the bile ducts.
glossary.Biliary tree: The whole branching network of bile ducts from liver to duodenum.
glossary.Gallstones: Hard deposits of cholesterol or pigment that form in the gallbladder.
glossary.Ascending infection: Infection travelling upwards from the gut into the bile ducts.
glossary.Causative organism: The microbe responsible for an infection.
glossary.Biliary surgery: Operations on the gallbladder or bile ducts.
glossary.RUQ: Right upper quadrant of the abdomen, over the liver and gallbladder.
glossary.Mental confusion: Disorientation or reduced alertness, here from sepsis.
glossary.GCS: Glasgow Coma Scale: scores eyes, voice and movement from 3 to 15.
glossary.Sepsis: Life-threatening organ dysfunction caused by a dysregulated response to infection.
glossary.Multi-organ failure: Failure of two or more organ systems, often the end stage of sepsis.
glossary.Diagnostic and therapeutic: Able both to find the problem and to treat it in the same procedure.
glossary.CRP: C-reactive protein: a blood marker of inflammation.
glossary.WCC: White cell count; raised in infection.
glossary.Bilirubin: Yellow breakdown product of haemoglobin, cleared in bile.
glossary.Cholestatic: Pattern of liver blood tests showing blocked bile flow, mainly raised ALP and GGT.
glossary.Abdominal ultrasound: Ultrasound of the abdomen; first look for stones and dilated ducts.
glossary.Dilated bile ducts: Bile ducts widened by pressure behind a blockage.
glossary.Non-invasive: Does not involve entering the body with instruments.
glossary.Delineate: To show the exact outline and position of something.
glossary.Biliary decompression: Draining the blocked bile ducts to relieve pressure.
glossary.ABCDE: Airway, Breathing, Circulation, Disability, Exposure: structured emergency assessment.
glossary.Ciprofloxacin: Quinolone antibiotic active against gut Gram-negative bacteria.
glossary.Penicillin allergy: Immune reaction to penicillin-type antibiotics, ruling out co-amoxiclav.
glossary.Stasis: Stagnation of a fluid that should be flowing.
glossary.Enteric organisms: Bacteria that normally live in the gut.
glossary.Toxins: Harmful molecules released by bacteria, such as endotoxin.
glossary.Encephalopathy: Brain dysfunction causing confusion or drowsiness.
glossary.Stenting: Placing a tube in a duct to hold it open.
glossary.Stone extraction: Removing a gallstone from the bile duct, usually with a balloon or basket at ERCP.
